yaml.title: LLM Inference & GPU Performance Engineer
yaml.description: Aman Pandey Sanjeev Kumar builds LLM inference runtimes, CUDA and Triton kernels, and reproducible compiler and performance benchmarks.

markdown.markdown:
I build efficient inference systems, from CUDA C++ and Triton kernels to LLM scheduling, KV-cache management, and compiler performance analysis. I hold an M.S. in Electrical and Computer Engineering from Purdue University (May 2026), specializing in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning. I am seeking **LLM Inference Engineer, Performance Engineer, and GPU Kernel Engineer** roles.

My work connects operator-level optimization with serving latency, throughput, and memory efficiency. I implement, validate against reference outputs, and profile before drawing conclusions. My benchmarks use explicit workload shapes, warmup and steady-state timing, and appropriate PyTorch or cuBLAS baselines; I investigate regressions as carefully as speedups.


- **[GPU kernels for LLM inference](projects/gpu-kernels.qmd):** FP32 RMSNorm and GEMV/small-M GEMM in CUDA C++ and Triton, including residual fusion that reduced seven eager PyTorch launches to one. Passed 80/80 backend-shape checks.
- **[nano-vLLM inference runtime](projects/runtime.qmd):** Continuous batching, chunked prefill, paged KV storage, and prefix caching. Measured 3.84x output throughput versus single-sequence scheduling on 12 mixed-length Qwen3-0.6B requests.
- **[PyTorch compiler performance](projects/dl-compilers.qmd):** FX capture, graph breaks, fusion, and correctness-checked LLM benchmarks. Reduced an eight-step Qwen2.5-0.5B FP32 decode from 97.9 to 66.8 ms with CUDA Graphs disabled.
- **[FlashAttention-2 in Triton](projects/transformers.qmd):** Forward attention with online softmax, FP16 MHA/GQA, and causal masking; validated 60/60 cases against PyTorch SDPA.
- **[MobileCLIP2 on Qualcomm QNN](projects/edge-ai.qmd):** PyTorch-to-ONNX-to-QNN deployment with 794/794 profiled operations on NPU and image/text P90 latencies of 14.51/3.99 ms on the S22 Family target.

## Background

At Purdue, I led IE 332 labs for 75 students covering machine learning, data pipelines, SQL, and backend development (August 2023 to December 2025). As a Data Science Researcher with Cisco and Purdue Data Mine (January to May 2024), I built forecast selection and ensembling methods for 10,000+ products, improving cost-weighted prediction accuracy by 3%.

My technical toolkit includes Python, C++, CUDA, Triton, CuTe DSL, CUTLASS, PyTorch, torch.compile, and ONNX. I use PyTorch Profiler, Nsight Systems, Nsight Compute, and Perfetto to connect runtime behavior to hardware bottlenecks, with additional interests in MLIR, XLA, TVM, quantization, and distributed inference.
